finish.summary:
I built a two-cell, two-storey workbench organizer with bins on top, drawers below and solid end caps on the open edges. It's 34 parts. check_build passes with no rule issues, and the mesh-collision check is clear.

- **Ground storey:** two north-half bases, each with a drawer on its cut face.
- **Top storey:** two more north-half bases standing on them. The configurator only takes a half base on top of a half base. One holds a full-height bin with 3 sections and the other a full-height bin with 2 sections.
- **Finishing:** I capped every open edge and bolted the joints together.
- **Props (staging only, not part of the build):** a hex driver, a marker and a pencil stand in the 3-section bin. Small heaps of screws and standoffs sit in the 2-section bin. They sit below the rim, so you only see them from above.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
